# Bank Transfer Process Plan

Plans a clause’s transfer policy for a document matching **Bank Transfer Contract**. It combines inherited connection planning with an optional condition that automatically requests the instruction’s single bank transfer. A request records an intention; transferred money requires a separate guarantor confirmation.

## Configuration

- `parameters.method` defaults to `bank-transfer`; only `bank-transfer` and `conditional-bank` are accepted. This validates the clause parameter, rather than changing `paymentTerms.method`.
- `parameters.transfer` defaults to `{}`. Its `mode` defaults to `workflow`; the only other supported value is `when`.
- In `workflow` mode, the plan returns the inherited connection plan without adding the conditional gate or automatic transfer handlers. Existing transfer-request checks still apply.
- In `when` mode, `parameters.transfer.when` must exist and `parameters.transfer.requestId` must be nonempty text. Execution additionally limits the identifier to 128 characters. The identifier correlates the single request and its outcomes.
- `parameters.sources` defaults to `{}` and declares aliases used by condition reads beneath `/sources/`. An undeclared alias is rejected.

The condition must have statically discoverable, pure dependencies. Supported operators are `$document`, `$nodeBlueId`, comparisons, Boolean operators, `$exists`, `$includes`, `$size`, `$add`, `$subtract` and `$literal`, with `list` and `val` operand fields. Document reads must use literal, non-root JSON pointers; `$nodeBlueId` must directly wrap one document read. Unsupported operators, dynamic paths and expressions exceeding the bounded 33-level scan are rejected.

`validateTransition` always refuses with `PAYMENT_PROCESS_POLICY_IMMUTABLE`. The supplied clause host consults existing clauses during amendments, so this refusal can also block an amendment that leaves this clause unchanged.

## Conditional requests

In `when` mode, the plan contributes `/paymentProcess_{clauseKey}/transferAllowed`, initially `false` when that state is created, and sets `/paymentTerms/transferGate` to that path. A pre-existing gate pointing elsewhere causes `PAYMENT_POLICY_GATE_CONFLICT`.

Generated handlers reevaluate the gate on changes to `/payment`, `/bankTransfer`, `/activation`, `/sourceLinks` and every discovered condition path. When `parameters.sources` is nonempty, an embedded-node handler also runs the same steps. The gate becomes true only when:

- `/activation/active` is exactly `true`;
- either `/clauses/documentSources` is absent or `/sourceLinks/ready` is exactly `true`;
- the configured `when` expression evaluates to exactly `true`.

After updating the gate, the handler attempts a request only if the gate is true, `/payment/accepted` is true, `/payment/closed` is false and `/bankTransfer/status` is `idle`. Otherwise, the request step has no effect. The generated request uses `sourceMode="event"` and the configured `requestId`, so it does not require a payer workflow call. A true gate alone does not establish a request or completion.

The underlying request function also checks source readiness and instruction acceptance. Public `requestTransfer` is bound to `payer` and checks the caller against `paymentTerms.payerChannel`. New requests reject a closed payment or a configured `transferGate` whose value is not true. After the source, actor, acceptance and identifier checks, reuse of the recorded identifier returns `duplicate`; a different identifier conflicts. This duplicate check precedes the closed-payment and gate checks.

A new request writes `/bankTransfer/requestId`, sets its status to `requested` and emits a Bank Transfer Event with `kind="Transfer Requested"`. Its amount and currency come exclusively from `paymentTerms.amountMinor` and `paymentTerms.currency`; callers supply neither. Payment initialization validates a positive integral amount, a nonempty currency and an integral `limitMinor` between the amount and 1,000,000,000,000.

## Outcomes and state

`requested` awaits a guarantor outcome. `unknown` remains unresolved and must be reconciled against the same request. `completed` and `declined` are terminal outcomes. The automatic handler requires `idle` before requesting, but the supplied definitions do not show the initialization of that bank-transfer state.

The public outcome operations are `confirmTransfer`, `declineTransfer` and `reportTransferUnknown`, bound to `guarantor`; recording also checks `paymentTerms.guarantorChannel`. They require the recorded `requestId` and a nonempty bank `reference` of at most 256 characters. Confirmation additionally requires `amountMinor` and `currency` to match the payment terms exactly. Declined and unknown reports may omit those fields and do not establish transferred money.

An identical status and reference returns `duplicate` after the applicable input checks. A changed reference for the same status conflicts. Otherwise, outcomes may be recorded only from `requested` or `unknown`; terminal outcomes cannot be replaced.

A newly recorded outcome updates `/bankTransfer/status` and `/bankTransfer/reference` and emits `Transfer Outcome`. Only completion sets `/payment/completed` to the instruction amount, copies the bank reference into `/payment/transactionId` and emits Payment Completed with `evidence="bankConfirmation"`. Completion does not itself set `/payment/closed`. This bank flow creates no card authorization or capture reservation; a refund is a separate transfer instruction.

All these paths belong to the executing bank-transfer instruction, including when it is nested in another document. Shared payment initialization sets `accepted`, `rejected` and `closed` to false and `completed` to zero. Missing values remain unknown; they do not establish those defaults, an idle transfer or rejection. Public bank workflows also invoke `Require Active Parties`; its underlying `requireActive` checks are not supplied.

## Inherited connections

Connection planning combines type `defaultBindings` with clause `bindings`, with clause entries taking precedence. Actions come from type `actions`, or `parameters.actions` when `configurableActions` is true. Property bindings are checked against declared `bindingTypes`; this planning definition supplies no concrete data-binding names.

Configured connections support `workflow`, `event`, `channel`, `embedded`, `collection`, `change`, `initialized`, `activated` and `timer` sources. Connection `params` override action `defaults`; `when` defaults to true, `once` to false, and `parameters.conditions` adds action-specific requirements. Workflow connections require an authenticated channel name. Optional `before` and `after` steps surround the action. For preflight and `outcome-v1` actions, only `acceptedNew` proceeds through the remaining steps; `duplicate`, `rejected` and `skipped` stop them. A `once` marker records completion of the connection body, not external transfer confirmation.

Timer connections use either an absolute `timestamp` in Unix microseconds or `afterEvent` with positive integral `delayMs`. Relative timers default to `policy="first"`; `latest` replaces the pending keyed timer on later triggers. `cancelOn` can request cancellation. Emitting a timer request does not establish that it fired.
